title: Pluscuamperfecto: lo que ya había ocurrido

sections.content: The pluperfect (había + participle) marks something that had already happened before another past moment -- essential here, where debt peonage only makes sense once you know the land privatization laws that made it possible came first. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Este sistema de deudas no había surgido de la nada: se apoyaba en las leyes liberales de privatización de tierras.
items.english: This debt system hadn't arisen out of nowhere: it rested on the liberal land-privatization laws.

items.spanish: Estas leyes ya habían despojado a muchas comunidades indígenas de sus tierras comunales.
items.english: These laws had already stripped many indigenous communities of their communal lands.

items.spanish: Millones de inmigrantes europeos habían llegado ya, hacia finales del siglo, atraídos por la demanda de mano de obra.
items.english: Millions of European immigrants had already arrived, toward the end of the century, drawn by the demand for labor.

items.spanish: Para 1900, un pequeño número de familias había acumulado ya extensiones de tierra prácticamente inimaginables décadas antes.
items.english: By 1900, a small number of families had already accumulated stretches of land practically unimaginable decades before.

sections.content: Ya (already) pairs naturally with the pluperfect to stress that the earlier event was fully complete by the later reference point -- habían llegado ya, había acumulado ya -- and can move around the sentence without changing its meaning.
